patient.name: Elena Castillo
patient.chiefComplaint: Vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain after motor vehicle collision, 32 weeks pregnant

history.hpi: Restrained driver involved in a moderate-speed T-bone collision approximately 20 minutes ago; airbag deployed. Since the crash, patient reports constant, severe lower abdominal pain and has noted vaginal bleeding soaking through her clothing. Denies loss of consciousness. Reports decreased fetal movement over the last several minutes.
medications: Labetalol 100 mg PO BID for gestational hypertension
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch approximately 3 hours prior to the collision
history.events: T-bone MVC as restrained driver; airbag deployed; bystanders called 911 immediately

scene.dispatch: 32-year-old female, motor vehicle collision, conscious, complaining of abdominal pain
scene.location: Intersection, patient's sedan struck on driver's side door, moderate intrusion
scene.safety: Vehicle stable, scene secured by police, no fuel leak
scene.bystanders: Passenger from other vehicle uninjured; witnesses report moderate-speed impact
visualCues: Visible blood staining on driver's seat and patient's clothing
Moderate door intrusion on driver's side

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 33-year-old, 32-weeks-pregnant female still in the driver's seat, alert and in visible distress with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is currently supine/semi-reclined in the seat.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mildly tachypneic, nonlabored, symmetric chest rise
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but rapid, skin pale and cool
otherFindings: Rigid, tender lower abdomen with a firm, board-like uterus
Reports decreased fetal movement over the last several minutes
No head strike, no loss of consciousness
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Something's wrong with my baby, my stomach won't stop hurting."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey to rule out other life threats before focusing on OB findings
expectedActions.rationale: Post-MVC patients need a structured trauma survey even when the OB presentation is prominent.

expectedActions.shortAction: Position patient left lateral recumbent given third-trimester shock
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If signs of shock or orthostasis: Position patient supine or in the left lateral recumbent position if third trimester and keep patient warm
expectedActions.rationale: Left lateral positioning relieves aortocaval compression from the gravid uterus, improving venous return.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish large-bore IV; begin crystalloid resuscitation, 1-2 L wide open
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Place large bore IV. Volume resuscitation: crystalloid 1–2 liters IV wide open
expectedActions.rationale: Aggressive volume resuscitation is indicated for suspected abruption with hemorrhagic shock, which may be concealed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Save all passed vaginal tissue/pads for receiving team assessment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Save all possible tissue so that the receiving team can assess
expectedActions.rationale: Passed tissue and blood loss quantity inform the receiving OB team's assessment.

transitions.if: Left lateral positioning and IV fluids started
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes signs of shock in a third-trimester patient, positions her in the left lateral recumbent position, and establishes large-bore IV access with crystalloid resuscitation.
Crew fails to maintain the patient in the left lateral position during packaging and transport, allowing the gravid uterus to compress the inferior vena cava.

phases.name: Left lateral positioning and IV fluids started
phases.description: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey, positions the patient in the left lateral recumbent position to relieve aortocaval compression, establishes large-bore IV access, and begins rapid crystalloid resuscitation.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing signs of shock with a rigid, tender uterus and vaginal bleeding in a third-trimester trauma patient, the crew positions her left lateral, secures IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation while preserving any passed tissue for the receiving team.

otherFindings: 18-gauge IV established in the left forearm
Ongoing vaginal bleeding, soaked pads preserved
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay, that does feel a little easier to breathe."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and response to fluid resuscitation serially en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess vital signs and response to fluid resuscitation
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing concealed hemorrhage can recur even after initial improvement.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport emergently to closest appropriate facility; notify en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Disposition – transport emergently to closest appropriate receiving facility – notify en route if possible so the receiving team may prepare
expectedActions.rationale: Advance notification allows the OB/trauma team to prepare for emergent delivery if needed.

transitions.condition: Vital signs trend toward normal after fluid resuscitation and left lateral positioning; crew initiates emergent transport with advance notification to the receiving OB unit.

phases.name: Perfusion improves, transport initiated
phases.description: Vital signs trend toward normal with fluid resuscitation and left lateral positioning. Crew reassesses serially and transports emergently to the closest appropriate obstetric/trauma-capable facility with advance notification.
phases.triggerCondition: After fluid resuscitation and left lateral positioning, the patient's perfusion improves; the crew reassesses vitals and initiates rapid transport with advance hospital notification.

otherFindings: Uterus remains firm and tender but bleeding has slowed
Advance notification given to receiving OB unit

phases.name: Left lateral positioning not maintained
phases.description: The patient is packaged and transported supine. Without left lateral tilt, the gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava, causing a sudden drop in venous return and worsening hypotension despite ongoing fluid resuscitation.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew maintains the patient supine during packaging and transport instead of left lateral recumbent, and she develops sudden worsening hypotension and tachycardia consistent with supine hypotensive syndrome from aortocaval compression.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy all of a sudden..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize supine hypotension; reposition left lateral or manually displace uterus left
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients in third trimester of pregnancy should be transported on left side or with uterus manually displaced to left if hypotensive
expectedActions.rationale: Aortocaval compression from a supine gravid uterus is a rapidly reversible cause of shock.
